body: Since signal can now be connected and called on the main thread, shouldn't it set the return value before `post`, otherwise `Thread::suspend` can return before it's set.
That is a very good point, thanks for pointing this out! Will change it.
In fact, it should be at the bottom so, if there is a call error, it wont post the semaphore.
Why returning an error instead of an Array with all arguments like `await` works with several arguments?
shouldn't this be an automatic check using `if (!Thread::is_in_main_thread()) {` instead of  passing an argument and leave it to user's discression?

i would add a ward here:
`ERR_COND_V(!Thread::is_main_thread(), "Cannot suspend main thread", ERR_UNNAVAILABLE);`
Actually, if you put [this guard](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103896#discussion_r1989664550), this if condition is not even needed, you will always connect on main thread
Thats a good point, I feel it may be a little error prone to do this, but if this is the prefererd behavior it should be no problem to do it.
You would be surprised how oddly people uses this stuff and await, I think its better to do it explicitly and let the user choose to do this.
I thought about it, I think you are right and will add this and eventually if anyone complains remove it.
I added it, simpler for consistency.

+				This function will fail if called from the main thread.

body:
"the function"? Which one?

"This is the thread that runs game code" is too reductive in my opinion, especially for anyone that knows what a "thread" even is in the first place. And they would need to know, otherwise the explanation wouldn't make sense to them.

I assume the following is correct, but this could use a bit more explanations and providing just a few common cases where this method can return `false`. I cannot provide myself.
```suggestion
				Returns [code]true[/code] if this function is called on the main thread of the engine. By default, the main thread runs most of the engine's logic.
```

body:
A script... awaits for "_something_"? But the signal to resume "_it_"...? From "_another_" what?

Also, these warnings are exposed as settings _because_ they may not always apply, so reminding that they can be disabled is quite redundant.
```suggestion
			If [code]true[/code], produces a warning when a script awaits for a signal in a thread, but the signal to resume the script originated from another thread. This behavior is usually unintentional.
```
That's with the assumption that it's correct. I haven't looked at prior discussion.
Does this warning only affect GDScript? If yes, it needs to be explicitly said, and the wording needs to be more specific. Also, in GDScript you can `await` for Callables so this may not be accurate. 

Also, the description really owes an explanation as to why this behaviour is undesirable. I assume it's because of confusion?
